frank-cs: Heads-up: ACME reported prod-quant-1 (4-bit) is slower and lower quality vs their fp16 baseline. p95 ~3x, some responses are garbled. Ticket 7891.
ingrid: Yikes. Did they change model or config? Any recent deployments?
frank-cs: No deploys on their side. They gave a sample prompt + trace link: https://acme.example/trace/7891 (internal link)
frank-cs: Sample prompt short: "Summarize the clinical trial results and list limitations." Latency spike visible around 2026-10-12T14:10Z.
ben-runtime: I'm running a local repro against redwood/llm-small-4bit with the same prompt.
ben-runtime: Quick profile (dev machine):
```
kv_cache_miss_rate: 42%
kernel_switch_count: 262341
avg_kernel_switch_latency_ms: 8.6
4bit_kernel_exec_ms: 6.1
fp16_kernel_exec_ms: 4.0
```
ben-runtime: Observed a lot of kernel selector churn: requests alternate between 4-bit fast path and fallback fp16 kernels because kv cache layout differs per request.
alice-ml: Could calibration have introduced a changed KV layout/stride? We recently added per-token scale metadata in the cache for quantized models.
eva: Reproduced with our repro harness. Root cause hypothesis: quant calibration metadata plus padded sequences produce non-contiguous KV tensor shapes. Kernel selector sees mismatched stride and routes to a slower compatibility kernel (fp16 path) for many steps, causing both latency and occasional output drift.
carla: Temporary mitigation: pin the customer's endpoint to fp16 until we fix selector or ensure consistent kv_layout. I can push a config change: \`model_override=fp16\` for prod-quant-1.
frank-cs: Please do that and tell ACME. They'll accept fp16 fallback for a short window.
ben-runtime: Created a repro script: `python repro_kv_churn.py --model redwood/llm-small-4bit --prompt samples/acme1.txt --seq 1024 --steps 64` This toggles the padding to force the misclassify.
ben-runtime: Attached flamegraph link (internal): https://perf.redwood/fg/1891234567
ingrid: Thanks. Can you also add a short warmup to keep kernels resident? e.g., warmup_count=20, persistent_kernel=true
ben-runtime: Yes, warmup reduces cold-switch penalties but doesn't fully fix misrouting. Need selector change.
eva: Candidate fix in PR #4532: selector will check explicit `kv_layout` metadata flag (rather than inferring from stride) and allow unified 4-bit kernel if flag matches. Unit tests added.
carla: Rolling fp16 pin now for prod-quant-1. ETA ~8m. Informing CS to notify ACME: "Temporary fallback to fp16 while we deploy a targeted fix; perf should return to baseline."
frank-cs: ACME updated: appreciates quick response, asked for ETA on full fix.
alice-ml: Estimated QA + canary for PR #4532 ~ 6-8 hours. We can try an accelerated canary for ACME tomorrow AM.
ingrid: Starting canary deploy of selector fix to canary pool (5% traffic) now. monitor hooks: p95, kernel_switch_count, kv_miss_rate.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for pr-4532 to cluster-canary-2.
ben-runtime: Canary metrics after 15m: p95 back to ~baseline, kernel_switch_count -92%, kv_miss_rate down to 6%.
deploy-bot: canary success criteria met. promoting to production rollout (gradual 25% -> 100%)
frank-cs: Updated ACME: fix deployed to canary and we're rolling it globally. We kept them on fp16 for safety during the first rollout window.
eva: Root cause summary for postmortem: quant calibration added per-token metadata that changed runtime tensor layout in some padding scenarios. Kernel selector used stride heuristics and misrouted many requests to a slower fp16 compatibility kernel. Fix: explicit kv_layout flag plus selector tolerance tests and a fallback warmup path.
carla: Closing loop: rolled customer to new selector, removed fp16 pin at 2026-10-12T18:30Z. Monitoring continues.
frank-cs: ACME acknowledged and will reopen if they see regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: prod rollout complete. Final metrics: p95 within 5% of baseline, error rate normalized.
